newsitem.title: USA: Standard holder files suit, demands records.
newsitem.headline: Standard holder files suit, demands records.

text.p: LaSalle/Kross Partners LP, which owns 5.4 percent of Standard Financial Inc, said Tuesday it filed a lawsuit in federal court and also "made demand" on the thrift to inspect and copy stock records.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the partnership said the suit, filed in U.S. District Court in Chicago on January 21, was in opposition to the injunctive relief requested by Standard in its lawsuit filed December 9, 1996.
The partners also requested a current stockholder list of names and addresses in order to notify other stockholders of the pending litigation against them, the filing said.
LaSalle/Kross said the lawsuit against them by the thrift is without merit, is "frivolous and intended primarily for harassment" of the partnership.
LaSalle/Kross said it holds the stake in the thrift for investment purposes.

However, because of the litigation filed against them, the partnerhip said they will not make any further purchases prior to the court's decision on Standard's motion for preliminary injunction or February 1, 1997 whichever comes first.
Standard Financial is a holding company for Standard Federal Bank for Savings of Chicago. It currently operates 14 full-service offices.
